content:
The right walking aid can make you safer.

This guide compares sticks and frames. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Sticks

  • Light support.
  • Use in the hand opposite the painful leg.

Frames

  • More support for balance.
  • Wheeled or non-wheeled types.

Using a frame indoors

  • Clear routes and rugs.
  • Check doorways and turning space.
  • Do not carry things in your hands; use a bag or tray on the frame.

Getting assessed

Ask your GP or physiotherapist.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I buy my own?

Yes, but get advice on height.

What about rollators?

They suit some people outdoors.
